questions.question: Two reviewers independently found that note 7 ("shared decisions most often retrofitted") and Q4's Retries row went to OP-01 only. But shared.md gives missing-key delete to OP-10's flow, a streamed-write exception to OP-03's flow, and retry to each entry's AX-13. Retries also names "GCS retries deletes by default". The agreed scope sent Q4's shared rows and note 7 to OP-01 only. How should those passages be routed?

options.label: Route by shared.md (Recommended)
options.description: Note 7 is also copied into OP-03 and OP-10, and the Retries row into OP-10. The rule becomes: a passage goes to every entry whose operation it names, or that shared.md makes its home. That rule is stated in BACKLOG-DONE. Error taxonomy, Timeouts and Consistency stay OP-01-only (shared.md homes them in OP-01's flow and RFC-0027 P3). Retries for every other entry's AX-13 is not copied 24 times.

options.label: Keep OP-01 only, state why
options.description: No files change. BACKLOG-DONE and the trace state that note 7 and Q4's cross-cutting rows go to OP-01, the first session, and that later sessions read shared.md for their home. That narrows the "each input file with a § 2 finding" claim. OP-10 and OP-03 sessions then never see the evidence.

options.label: Copy all Q4 rows by name
options.description: Apply 'names the operation' to every Q4 row as well. Consistency's "atomic put" goes to OP-03 and OP-04, and "list may miss recent writes" to OP-06 and OP-07, on top of the recommended routing. This widens the PR, and judging which row names which operation invites further rounds.

options.label: Enumerated table in trace (Recommended)
options.description: Replace the prose rule in BACKLOG-DONE with a pointer to a passage-to-entries table in the trace, one row per § 2 passage with its reason, checked by script against the files. The Consistency row also goes to OP-03, OP-06 and OP-07 (put, list). Ends the argument by making every routing call visible.

options.label: Narrow the prose rule
options.description: Restate the rule as the one actually applied (Q1 by catalogue Form-of, others by the entries their label names or shared.md homes), and leave Consistency in OP-01 only. Smallest change; OP-06/07 sessions miss the list-after-write fact.

options.label: Stop routing, link research
options.description: Drop the claim of complete routing: each file says the full § 2 is in the research doc, which /observe may name. Contradicts BK-497's premise that sessions can't read it.

questions.question: The rule for which § 2 passages go into which input file has been refuted four rounds running. How should it be settled?

options.label: Literal rule, script-enumerated (Recommended)
options.description: Q1 rows go where the catalogue's Not in v1 table disposes them. Every other passage goes to each entry whose ID or operation word it contains, using a lexicon listed in the trace. Note 7 also goes where shared.md homes it, and Q4 rows that name no operation go to OP-01. A script builds the passage→entries table into the trace and asserts it against the files. About 14 more copies (Q2 write bullet to OP-01/10/12/13/20, Consistency row to OP-03/04/06/07, and others), and the OP-16 `..` copy is dropped as spec 052's. The routing becomes checkable, which ends the loop.

options.label: Table of current routing
options.description: No files change. The prose rule is replaced by a per-passage table in the trace stating the basis each copy actually had, and BACKLOG-DONE points to it. The table is honest, but it records judgement calls (e.g. the Q2 write bullet not in OP-12/13), so another round may question them.

options.label: Narrow to IDs only
options.description: Copy only where a passage or its § 2 heading names the entry by OP-ID, Q1 rows by catalogue disposition, and note 7 by shared.md home. This reverts the operation-word copies from rounds 1 and 3 (Q3 gates in OP-05/07/12/13, Retries in OP-10). The rule is simplest, but sessions lose evidence they had.

Round 5 hit the 5-round ceiling with one low-severity finding: a trace extract says "notes 2 to 6" where note 1 also names an entry. How should the loop close?

options.label: Fix, verify, close (Recommended)
options.description: Push the one-word fix. Then run one verification panel on the new head: an unprimed pass plus a whole-file pass (the stop rule needs both on the final state; the change asserts no behaviour, so no measuring pass). If both are clean, the loop closes and I write the Step 5 close: review block, report and decision-log tail.

options.label: Fix and keep reviewing
options.description: Push the fix and run a full round 6 panel (unprimed, measuring, whole-file) as usual. Costs one more panel; useful only if you expect more defects than the trend suggests.

options.label: Stop here, fix in close
options.description: Fold the one-word fix into the Step 5 close commit with no further review. Cheapest, but the loop would end on an unreviewed fix pass, which the stop rule forbids, so you'd be waiving that rule for this PR.
